A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same graph-based reasoning-data synthesis work, renamed from GSDP to GRIP. The main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite extensive revision and reorganization.

before.justification: v2 reports original fine-tuning and continued-pretraining results, model-combination experiments, component ablations, and appendix analyses of synthetic-data similarity and diversity.

after.justification: v4 reports original model evaluations, human-labeled filtering validation, ablations, AIME results, and appendix analyses of contamination, concept adherence and dataset scale.

M1.justification: The graph backbone remains, but v4 replaces extraction, generation and evaluation models with newer Qwen2.5-family and DeepSeek-based components. It reduces the extraction limit from ten concepts to five, expands community combinations from three concepts to three or four, and introduces stated filtering of low-weight implicit combinations. These substantially revise the described pipeline beyond renaming.

E1.justification: The principal mathematical and six scientific benchmarks remain; GPQA already used the Diamond subset in v2. v4 adds AIME 2024. The full MMLU and C-Eval evaluations associated with v2's pretraining experiment are no longer reported, although their benchmark descriptions remain in v4 Appendix C.

E2.justification: v4 Table 2 adds Qwen2-Math variants, DeepSeekMath-Instruct/RL and reproduced MathScale-Qwen1.5 results, while dropping GPT-4/GPT-3.5 and several older model rows. The scientific comparison removes WizardMath, MAmmoTH, MetaMath and MathScale despite retaining them elsewhere. The filtering experiment also replaces the older model combinations and introduces GPT-4.1 as an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: Fine-tuning maximum sequence length changes from 2048 to 4096, and the trained model configurations expand from three to six. v2's continued-pretraining protocol disappears. Filtering validation changes from 5,000 GPT-4-labeled samples to 500 human-labeled samples. v4 introduces volume-controlled ablations, AIME pass@64 and an 80K-sample comparison, and replaces clustering-based diversity measurement with concept-combination novelty.

E4.justification: v4 replaces the five-mixture component experiment with a size-controlled explicit-versus-implicit comparison and adds hop-distance/hub, concept-filtering, contamination, reverse concept-extraction and small-dataset analyses. The earlier community-contribution comparison and DBSCAN diversity analysis disappear. The 26%-to-45% dual-filtering finding remains in Appendix D and is not a new result.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated training runs, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. Both principally report point estimates. The new pass@64 evaluation specifies inference sampling rather than adding uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Under revised synthesis and training settings, Mistral-based MATH/GSM8K scores change from 37.7/78.4 in v2 Table 1 to 41.6/83.5 in v4 Table 2. Reported expansion changes from 255-fold to 280-fold and per-sample cost from 1.23 to 0.57 in units of 0.01 cents. Numerous model and diagnostic results are added; pretraining, clustering and earlier precision/recall/retention results disappear.

T1.justification: The community-combination definition broadens from three mutually connected concepts to three- or four-concept cliques. The explicit/implicit-edge and shortest-path definitions otherwise remain mathematically equivalent. Neither version supplies theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The central claims of scalable, diverse and inexpensive graph-based synthesis remain. The dataset contribution changes from 1.91 million to 2.1 million pairs, and v4's conclusion explicitly qualifies applicability beyond mathematical synthesis as unverified. These are bounded revisions to the retained contribution.

C2.justification: Appendices E–F add substantive interpretations of contamination checks, concept adherence and comparisons at controlled dataset size. v4 explicitly limits validated synthesis applicability to mathematics and discusses adapting concept definitions for structured and commonsense domains. It also discusses high-hop quality/cost tradeoffs, while v2's pretraining-based interpretation about preserving general abilities disappears.

D1.justification: v4 specifies revised component models and synthesis resources: eight A100 GPUs for 36 hours versus eight RTX 4090 GPUs for 84 hours. It documents normalization and reverse-extraction procedures for new analyses. However, Appendix A shrinks from six prompt templates to two, omitting clustering, solution-generation and both evaluation prompts; the promised dataset/model release location also disappears.

R1.justification: v4 adds literature on data-constrained scaling, data exhaustion, chain-of-thought, DeepSeek-R1 and Qwen2.5-family models, while removing several continued-pretraining references. Positioning shifts toward data scarcity and opaque specialist-data pipelines, but the central contrast with seed rewriting and explicit-only concept synthesis remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, method explanations and results narrative are extensively rewritten. Related work moves before the method, dataset comparisons become a method subsection, and the appendices are reorganized and expanded. Terminology changes throughout from GSDP/KP/KPRG to GRIP/KC/KCRG, alongside title and author-information edits.

P2.justification: v4 replaces the opening scatterplots with a comparison schematic, redraws the pipeline and graph figures, and consolidates four appendix similarity plots into main-text Figure 4. Results tables gain base-model and size columns, scientific results move into the main text, and new ablation and appendix tables substantially change the visual organization.

improvement.justification: Compared with v2's component-mixture experiment and GPT-4 reference labels, v4 provides stronger validation through explicit data-volume controls and human labels, supplemented by contamination/adherence checks and specific domain limitations. However, prompt and release details disappear, and some interpretations overstate the evidence: Section 4.4 claims universal scientific gains despite Qwen2-1.5B's BBH decline from 36.8 to 35.2 in Table 3. These tradeoffs limit the net quality improvement.
